title: Review of c53's vortex-dipole negative on fresh seeds 46 and 47: vortices with an opposite-sign partner move no faster than others (median 0.022/0.019 vs 0.021/0.020 same-sign and 0.020/0.019 alone, sqrt(area) per t); 3 of 5 dividing vortices travel 3 lengths, 1 of them mostly in a dipole
summary: Labkit runs of the fed-vortex claim's world.py (defaults) on seeds 46 and 47, 128^2, 1000 frames x 150 steps (t=3000), read with the finding's dipmove.py. Median frame-step speed in sqrt(area) per t, by nearest neighbour within 2.5 sqrt(area): opposite sign 0.0219 / 0.0195, same sign 0.0206 / 0.0196, none 0.0201 / 0.0187 (n 15017/10678/1487 and 15273/10219/1568 steps). Dividing vortices (born by a persistent split, ending in one): 2 and 3; travelling 3 sqrt(area) between birth and division 1 and 2, the same in long axes; mostly in a dipole 0 and 1; median share of life with a dipole partner 0.16 and 0.64.

observations.M: dipmove_s46.json, dipmove_s47.json: opposite-sign medians within 7% of same-sign and lone medians on both seeds; dividing vortices that travel 3 lengths: 1 of 2 and 2 of 3, of which 0 and 1 mostly in a dipole

controls_run.M: same-sign and lone steps in the same runs (the finding's internal comparison)

verdicts.limitation: Only 5 dividing vortices on two seeds, so the 3-length share (3 of 5 here, 3 of 18 in the finding) is noisy. One seed-47 vortex that passes spends most of its life in a dipole, so dipole travel can occasionally carry a dividing vortex. The main result, that pairing does not raise speed in the dividing regime, holds.
